Health & Fear

Health & Fear

Damage does not only bring a character closer to defeat.
It also reduces how much of their full potential they can still bring into a roll.

Your Vitality determines the size of your Health Bars.
Each Health Bar represents a deeper stage of injury.

Determining Health Bars

By default, everyone has five Health Bars.

Each Health Bar has:

Vitality × 4 boxes by default. Passive: Fortitude may increase that multiplier to ×5, ×6, ×7, or ×8 at Power Levels 4, 8, 12, and 16, respectively, while slotted. It changes the maximum size of normal Health Bars only; it does not create additional bars, heal lost HP, or reopen Scarred bars. Passive: Health and Passive: Fortitude share the Health category and cannot be slotted together. Passive: Absorption does not grant HP.

After all available Health Bars are depleted (including any additional Bars granted by Growth or other approved effects), the character enters the Incapacitated state, which is represented by one final box.

  • Active Health Bar: the highest Health Bar that is not Scarred.
  • You can heal damage only within your current Active Health Bar.
  • Once a Health Bar is completely filled, it becomes Scarred.
  • A Scarred Health Bar cannot be healed during the same combat unless a rule explicitly allows it.
  • The final box is always Incapacitated.

Health Penalties

Health penalties reduce the number of dice you roll.

Health Healthy Bruised Injured Wounded Broken Incap.
Pool — −10% −20% −40% −50% no actions

Round dice loss down, minimum 0.

Applies to attacks, Attribute Checks, Skill Checks, spells, rituals, and initiative.
Does not reduce damage dice unless a rule explicitly says so.

Order of Pool Reduction

When multiple rules modify a dice pool, apply them in this order:

  1. Start with the relevant Attribute.
  2. Apply Skill training rules.
    • If the Skill is trained enough, use the full Attribute pool.
    • If the Skill is too low, use half the Attribute pool, rounded down.
  3. Apply all flat pool changes from range, environment, Powers, Stones, Buffs, Specials, Fear, or other effects. This includes Weaken, Soulburn, and a subtraction of 1 die for each point of Fear.
  4. Apply the current percentage-based Health Penalty to the remaining pool.
  5. Round the number of dice lost to the Health Penalty down.
  6. Reduce the final Pool no lower than 0 dice. A Pool of 0 fails automatically.
  7. Roll the remaining dice and keep up to Mastery Rank dice (or all of them if fewer remain), unless a rule explicitly modifies Keep.

Flat pool reductions, including accumulated Fear, are applied before the percentage-based Health Penalty. If multiple flat reductions apply to the same roll, add them together before calculating the Health Penalty. Fear reduces Attribute-based roll pools, not Damage Dice or the Mastery-Rank-based Initiative dice; it never reduces Keep.

Example

Someone with Vitality 2 has the following Health Levels.

Each normal Health Bar has:

Vitality × 4 = 8 boxes

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Healthy [Vitality × 4] (No penalty)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Bruised [Vitality × 4] (−10% dice pool)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Injured [Vitality × 4] (−20% dice pool)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Wounded [Vitality × 4] (−40% dice pool)

[ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ] - Broken [Vitality × 4] (−50% dice pool)

[ ] - Incapacitated

Pool Reduction Example

A character has Agility 16, Mastery Rank 3, and is making a Stealth check. Their Stealth Skill is high enough to use the full Attribute Pool, but they are affected by Weaken(4) and are currently Injured.

  1. Attribute Pool = 16
  2. Skill trained enough → full pool = 16
  3. Weaken(4) removes 4 dice → 12 dice remain
  4. Injured Health Penalty removes 20% of 12 → lose 2 dice
  5. Final Pool = 10k3

If the same character were Wounded, the 40% Health Penalty would remove 4 dice from the post-Weaken pool of 12.

Final Pool = 8k3

Healing and Scarred-Bar Restoration

Healing has two distinct jobs: restore HP in the current active Health Bar or return a lost Scarred Health Bar to full strength. Each job has its own source and resource.

  • HP Healing: Resolve Stone Ability: Healing heals Self or one ally with 4d8 / 8d8 / 12d8 / 16d8 at Ranks 1-4, within 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 m. Damage Transfer heals its user by actual HP removed from an enemy. End-of-combat and rest recovery refill HP at their stated times.
  • Current Bar: Ordinary HP Healing fills the current active Bar up to its maximum. A living Incapacitated or Stable character who receives positive legal HP Healing reopens Broken and places those HP there, as detailed under Incapacitation & Death.
  • Restoring Scarred Bars: Restoration Actives, Passive: Regeneration (Self), Vitality: Remove Scar, and specified natural, ritual or Artifact effects return Scarred Bars unscarred and at full current HP. Each source spends its printed Scarred-Bar resource. Partially damaged, already available Bars retain their existing HP; damage stays on the Bar where it occurred.
  • Recovery order: Recover the lowest eligible Scarred Bar first, progressing toward Healthy. Recover Broken first when an Incapacitated character needs an available Bar. A specific recovery rule, such as a hidden Growth Bar rule, may specify a different eligible choice. Recalculate the highest available Bar and all applicable Health penalties after recovery.
  • Resource cycles: Each Restoration Power has one finite pool per Safe Haven Rest; several uses draw from that same pool. Regeneration spends its own Self-only allowance per Tyhran Day. A Safe Haven Rest itself naturally returns exactly one Scarred Bar, independently of any Restoration Points the player later chooses to spend.

Restoration works with whole Bars and their full HP capacity; Resolve Healing works with rolled HP and the current Bar. Consult Actives and Passives for the level tables, legal targets and action timing.

Incapacitation & Death

When all of your Health Bars are fully depleted, your body collapses under the weight of battle.

You are now Incapacitated.

Incapacitated

  • You fall Prone.
  • You cannot take Attack Actions, Reactions, or Movement.
  • You begin with 0 Death Marks.
  • At the end of each of your turns, the GM rolls your Death Check. (The roll may be kept secret for dramatic effect.)

Death Check

Use the higher of your Vitality or Resolve.

Roll dice equal to that Attribute and keep dice equal to your Mastery Rank.

Death Check TN = (8 × your Mastery Rank) − 2

A Death Check is a special Attribute Check.

  • Skill Points cannot be spent on it.
  • Vitality cannot be spent after the roll.
  • Health penalties do not reduce the Death Check Pool.
  • Fear does not reduce the Death Check Pool.
  • Only an effect that explicitly modifies Death Checks can change the result.
Result Effect
Success You remain Incapacitated and mark 1 Success.
Failure You gain 1 Death Mark (Failure).

Track both Successes and Death Marks separately:

  • At 4 Successes, you are Stabilized.
  • At 4 Death Marks, you die.

Stabilized

Once 4 Successes are reached or an ally stabilizes you, you are Stable.

  • You remain Unconscious at 0 Health Bars.
  • You no longer roll Death Checks.
  • You remain at 0 boxes and do not awaken until healing or recovery restores you.
  • Positive legal HP Healing or external Scarred-Bar Restoration that creates an available Bar with positive HP awakens you immediately; ordinary stabilization by itself does not.
A living **Incapacitated or Stable** character who receives **positive HP Healing from Resolve or another explicitly permitted HP-healing exception** immediately reopens **Broken**, applies that healing there and regains consciousness with positive HP; this works before stabilization. **External Restoration** can instead fully restore the required Scarred Bar (Broken first), ending Incapacitated/Stable when positive available HP is present. Passive Regeneration cannot be consciously activated by an Incapacitated creature. Neither operation revives a truly Dead creature. Incapacitated ends as soon as the creature has legal available HP again; the Death Check/Success/Death Mark tally for that incapacitation ends. A later incapacitation begins a new tally.

Healing & Assistance

An adjacent ally may:

  • Spend 1 Attack Action to make a Medicine Skill Check against a Difficult TN based on the patient’s Mastery Rank (TN = (12 × MR) − 2). On success, the patient is Stabilized (counts as 4 Successes).
  • Use legally prepared Resolve Stone Healing or a specifically allowed HP-healing exception to restore positive HP; alternatively use a legal external Restoration Active to fully restore Scarred Bars and regain positive available HP.
  • Passive: Regeneration is a conscious Self-only choice for a capable creature; while Incapacitated, recovery comes from an eligible external source.

When light touches flesh, even the dying remember what it means to breathe.

Falling Damage

A creature takes 1d8 Damage for every full 4 m fallen.

Distance Damage
0–3 m —
4–7 m 1d8
8–11 m 2d8
12–15 m 3d8
16–19 m 4d8

Continue this progression for greater distances.

Falling Damage ignores Armor.

Fear

Fear is an accumulating value that starts at 0. When an event or the GM calls for a Fear Check, each selected character rolls their Resolve Pool, keeping one die (Resolve k1). Use the same fixed result bands for ordinary, extreme and supernatural events. The GM chooses who is affected; the band is determined by the roll rather than Challenge MR or an adjustable Difficulty.

Resolve k1 result Fear gained
0-7 +2 Fear
8-15 +1 Fear
16 or higher +0 Fear

Applying Fear. Add the rolled Fear to the character's current total. Each point of Fear removes one die from Attribute-based Pools, including Martial Attack, Spell Casting, Skill, Attribute and Ritual Checks. Apply this flat reduction before percentage Health Penalties. The final Pool can reach 0 dice; a Fear Check made with 0 dice falls in the 0-7 band and gains +2 Fear. Keep, Damage Dice, Death Checks and MR-based Initiative Dice retain their normal values.

Recovery. Fear continues across scenes and combats. A Safe Haven Rest returns Fear to 0. Healing, Cleanse, Night Rest and Day of Rest resolve their own listed effects, leaving the Fear total in place.

Check procedure. A Fear Check uses Resolve k1 and the fixed table. Skill Points and Raises are not part of this check; existing Mental Restrictions apply according to their own rules.

::

Fear Check Examples

Example — Sudden horror: A character rolls Resolve k1 and keeps a 7. The result is below 8, so they gain 2 Fear.

Example — Unsettling revelation: Another character rolls Resolve k1 and keeps 15. The result falls within 8–15, so they gain 1 Fear.

Example — Holding steady: A third character keeps 16 (or more) and gains 0 Fear. The same bands apply whether the event was ordinary or supernatural; the GM does not select an alternate Fear TN.

Boundary results: 7 → +2, 8 → +1, 15 → +1, 16 → +0.

Accumulation: If a character begins the scene with Fear 2 and rolls an 8, they gain 1 Fear and now have Fear 3. With Resolve 8 and Fear 3, their Resolve-based Attribute Pool is 5 dice before any percentage Health Penalty. Fear remains until a Safe Haven Rest or an explicit future rule provides another way to remove it; the final Pool can reach 0 dice.
